significance.value: 3.3σ above the Standard Model prediction (Fermilab result alone); 4.2σ tension for the experimental average combined with earlier measurements

summary.plain: Fermilab's first result for the muon's magnetic anomaly, measured to 0.46 parts per million. The result is 3.3 standard deviations above the Standard Model prediction and in excellent agreement with the earlier Brookhaven measurement; combined with previous measurements, the tension between experiment and theory rises to 4.2 standard deviations.
summary.technical: First results of the Fermilab Muon g-2 Experiment: aμ(FNAL) = 116,592,040(54)×10⁻¹¹ (0.46 ppm), 3.3 standard deviations greater than the Standard Model prediction and in excellent agreement with BNL E821. Combined with previous measurements of both μ⁺ and μ⁻, the new experimental average is aμ(Exp) = 116,592,061(41)×10⁻¹¹ (0.35 ppm), which increases the tension between experiment and theory to 4.2 standard deviations.

title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm
why_it_matters: The paper compares the measured muon anomaly with the Standard Model prediction recommended by the Muon g−2 Theory Initiative: the Fermilab result alone is 3.3 standard deviations above it, and the new experimental average increases the tension between experiment and theory to 4.2 standard deviations.
